run_note: Monday 2026-08-24, 09:30Z. NO R1 BREACH. NO SIM-INTEGRITY ALERT on either defined test - every fill audited this run sits inside its day's low-high and every one was crypto, so the market-hours gate did not apply. But a NEW MARK-INTEGRITY FAULT leads, and it is the same family as the 07-22 stale-fill and 08-03 phantom-weekend-mark incidents. (1) hunter has been marking and ranking SOL-USD at the PREVIOUS UTC DAY'S CLOSE for nine hours. Its value sat at exactly 908.69 from 00:06Z to 07:01Z - 9.675882 SOL x 93.9125, SOL's 08-22 close - then snapped to exactly 923.49, SOL's 08-23 close, and froze again, while the crypto bot repriced XRP every single cycle. Cause: hunter's frame mixes equities with crypto, so trim_incomplete_bars drops the current weekday row while the equity columns are still NaN and takes the live crypto price with it; the function's own docstring names mixed frames as the case it does not handle. On Sunday the same bot marked SOL live all day, because weekend rows are deliberately kept - which is why this has been invisible on weekends. Effect: the book is overstated by 9.01 right now, and worse, its reward/risk ranker and stop are deciding on day-old prices for an asset that trades 24/7. That is how it bought SOL nine minutes off a high on 08-23. Reported, not touched. (2) The staleness check itself is CLEAN: all ten paper books are 14.5-14.7 minutes old in a tight cluster and lottery is 7 - no frozen bot. Note the distinction that matters: hunter's TIMESTAMP was fresh every cycle while its PRICE was a day old, so the 08-03 age-based check would never have caught this. (3) hypecrypto bought ENA-USD a second consecutive day and lost a second consecutive time, -7.79 after -55.30, which closes yesterday's skip call as a +7.79 win and makes it nine round trips in nine days with nine finishes below the start. Refiled a fourth time. (4) The double-instance fault recurred twice but both windows re-marked only; no trade was rewritten. (5) GitHub Actions breached the 90-minute cron rule again at 115.5 minutes, third day running, and the local loop covered every minute of it.

open_faults.fault: mixed-universe bots mark and rank their CRYPTO holdings at the previous UTC day's close on any US weekday before the equity feed lands
open_faults.status: OPEN, NEW this run, root cause identified
open_faults.detail: hunter_tracker.fetch() calls market_hours.trim_incomplete_bars() on a frame holding equities beside crypto. On a weekday whose equity columns are still all-NaN the function drops the whole trailing row - correct for the equities it was written for (2026-07-26), but it takes the LIVE crypto column down with it. Measured: hunter's mark sat at exactly 908.69 for seven straight hours (00:06Z-07:01Z), which is 9.675882 SOL x 93.9125 = SOL's 08-22 CLOSE, then snapped to exactly 923.49 = 9.675882 x 95.4422 = SOL's 08-23 CLOSE and froze again. Over the same hours the crypto bot repriced XRP every cycle because crypto_tracker uses crypto_prices.live(). On Sunday 08-23 hunter marked SOL live all day - weekend rows are deliberately kept by the trim - so the fault appears only on weekdays and disappears at the equity open. Impact now: recorded 923.49 vs a true 914.48, overstating the book by 9.01 (0.98%), and hunter's momentum/vol ranker and stop run on day-old prices for a 24/7 asset during the same window. The trim_incomplete_bars docstring already names mixed frames as the unhandled case and points at last_real_date(). NOT a fill fault: no recorded fill price is outside its day's range. Owner decides; supervisor does not touch code.

open_faults.detail: 36 bot.yml runs in 24h, 30 cancelled and 4 successful. Largest gap 115.5 minutes, 08-23T23:58:12Z to 08-24T01:53:44Z, over the 90-minute rule; four further gaps of 78.9, 74.5, 61.0 and 59.3 minutes. The local loop covered the whole breach window, committing at 00:01, 00:07, 00:08, 00:21, 00:35, 00:36, 01:02, 01:03, 01:30 and 01:41Z, so no mark or trade was missed. This is a hosted-cron reliability problem, not a fleet outage - the owner's external-trigger escalation still applies.
